page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor family. The server provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, lacking hardware hyperthreading for a clean 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation. It features 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps. No graphical processing units are integrated into this configuration.

Benchmark results highlight notable memory bandwidth and multi-threaded processing capabilities. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 405.8 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 184.15 GB/sec, placing the memory subsystem within the top tier. PassMark database operations and multi-core Geekbench performance both place in the top decile with scores of 47,362.41 and 21,506.0 respectively. Redis operations achieve 68.24 million SET operations per second. In contrast, single-core CPU metrics and stress-ng performance align with mid-range averages, and large model LLM text generation rates remain low due to CPU-only execution.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio paired with 1900 GB of bundled NVMe instance storage creates an efficient environment for operational memory density. For workloads that do not demand x86 instruction extensions or GPU acceleration, the dedicated ARM core structure minimizes thread contention while keeping infrastructure footprint consolidated.

The r8gd.8xlarge is best suited for memory-intensive workloads, enterprise databases, in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, large-scale software compilation, and high-throughput static web serving.

The instance includes no GPU. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier uncached memory read bandwidth at 405.8 GB/sec and top-tier PassMark database operations at 47,362.41, along with a top-decile multi-core Geekbench score of 21,506.0. While single-thread CPU performance remains in the middle percentile, the server demonstrates strong efficiency in parallelized memory-intensive operations. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, data processing pipelines, and large compilation tasks requiring substantial memory bandwidth and dedicated thread isolation.
